lines.text: ### Silva-Inspired Meditation for Focus, Confidence, and Self-Direction
As you exhale, allow your body to become heavier, quieter, and more relaxed.
For these next few moments, your only responsibility is to direct your own mind.
I’ll count slowly from **10 down to 1**.
With every number, your body relaxes while your mind becomes clearer.
**2.** Your attention becomes quiet and clear.
**1.** You are relaxed, awake, and aware.
Imagine yourself standing before a door.
You enter a quiet control room.
In front of you is a large mental screen.
There is no control labeled **Everything That Happens.**
You do not need control over everything.
You can choose where to place your attention.
You can choose what you mentally rehearse.
You can choose your next action.
Allow one worry, frustration, or limiting thought to appear on the screen.
It is not automatically a fact.
I can choose what happens next.**
Your mind does not have to obey every thought it produces.
Now see yourself on the screen.
See the next stronger version of yourself.
See yourself handling pressure without losing direction.
See yourself starting what needs to be started.
Solving problems one step at a time.
Feel the confidence that comes from knowing:
**I do not need every situation to be easy.
I can respond intelligently when things become difficult.**
Think of one goal that matters to you.
Keep moving backward until you reach one action you can take today.
Bring your thumb, index finger, and middle finger gently together.
**When I use this gesture, I remember this state.**
Whenever you use this gesture, let it remind you:
Return to what you can control.
I choose where I place it.**
I decide which thoughts deserve action.**
**My emotions can speak without becoming my commander.**
**I can experience uncertainty without surrendering my direction.**
**I visualize what I want to build.**
**I rehearse courage before courage is required.**
**I practice discipline before discipline is tested.**
**My past can teach me without controlling me.**
**My future can inspire me without distracting me from today.**
**This moment is where my power lives.**
See yourself moving through the rest of today with quiet confidence.
**4.** Decide what your first useful action will be.
